subject: Mapping retention tiers to residency options — risk matrix for DPA
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@stratushealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Stratus Health Legal <legal@stratushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Nov 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mapping retention tiers to residency options — request

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal team asked me to put together a short list of open items so we can close the DPA redline. The two asks that matter most for us: 1) a clear table that maps each retention tier (ephemeral debug, short-term logs, customer records, archived snapshots) to where the data physically lives under Redwood (hosted multi-region, customer-dedicated pools, on-prem/private), and 2) what proof we can provide for each tier on deletion (manifest, signed cert, audit log entry).

We'd prefer a single artifact that shows risk (likelihood of cross-border access), retention enforcement mechanism, and what operational evidence you will provide. Can Redwood produce that "risk matrix" and propose a small set of redline changes that let us accept the residency language without a long legal loop?

If helpful, loop in your engineering lead. We aim to finish this week.

Best,
Emma

Emma Li
Head of Vendor Risk, Stratus Health
emma.li@stratushealth.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma.li@stratushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Nov 2029 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mapping retention tiers to residency options — request

Emma — thanks, super helpful. I drafted a compact risk matrix and attached it (redwood-residency-risk-matrix-v1.xlsx) that maps the four retention tiers to our three hosting modes, shows the primary controls, and lists the form of deletion evidence we can provide. Key notes in the sheet:

- We treat ephemeral debug logs as transient (TTL < 72 hours) in hosted mode; deletion proof is a timestamped GC manifest and ephemeral bucket tombstone.
- Short-term logs are retained in customer-dedicated pools for US customers; deletion proof includes an audit log entry plus an MD5 manifest of deleted files.
- Customer records (PII-linked model inputs) can be pinned to Dedicated or Private deployments per the DPA; deletion proof is a signed erasure certificate with a correlated request ID and AuditTrail entry.
- Archived snapshots (cold tier) are subject to region pairing for durability; if a residency commitment is required we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated onshore replica.

I'm looping Laura for legal alignment on the suggested redline language and Rishi for an ops read on the requested deletion evidence. We'll avoid changing the core DPA structure — instead we propose an appendix (Risk & Evidence Matrix) that enumerates accepted proof types per tier. That approach preserves standard DPA semantics while giving your team the artifacts you need.

Can you confirm whether Stratus needs an onshore-only backup copy (separate from the primary) or if a dedicated onshore primary + encrypted cross-region snapshot with strict access controls would be sufficient? That will affect the wording in the matrix.

Talk soon — I pushed the file to the Drive link in case you need it now.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Nov 2029 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mapping retention tiers to residency options — request

Ben — quick notes on the legal side after a first pass at the matrix and redline doc (DPA_redlines_RB_marked.docx):

1) Appendix approach: I agree — adding an appendix that catalogs retention/residency/evidence reduces friction. We should be explicit that the appendix is informational and does not expand Redwood's access rights beyond the DPA.

2) Wording for deletion proof: replace "signed erasure certificate" with "signed erasure confirmation, consisting of a deletion manifest with request identifier and verifier signature" to avoid implying an irrevocable third-party certification.

3) Backups and snapshots: For onshore-only commitments, add a carve-out that allows disaster recovery-only cross-border failover under pre-agreed notice and a timeboxed hold; include a requirement for post-failover erasure confirmation.

4) Audit logs: we should limit the retention period for high-fidelity audit logs to 2 years in the appendix and note that aggregated telemetry used for performance tuning is stored separately with lower fidelity.

I left inline comments on the redline doc. Rishi — can you confirm our current ability to generate the MD5 manifests and the exact audit log fields (request ID, actor, timestamp, object path) so I can make the wording precise?

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Nov 2029 14:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mapping retention tiers to residency options — request

Quick ops confirmation:

- MD5 manifests: yes, we can emit per-commit manifests for file-based storage and per-blob tombstone entries for object stores. Those manifests include object path, size, checksum, and deletion timestamp.
- Audit log fields: we have request_id, actor_id (service or user), action, object_path, timestamp, region, and correlation_id.
- Signed erasure flow: we can generate an internal signed artifact (HSM-backed signature linked to the request_id) that includes the manifest and audit-log pointers. That satisfies most compliance requests. External notarization is not standard and would require an escrowed third-party process.
- Onshore-only backup: we can spin a dedicated onshore repository for Stratus but it changes provisioning and pricing.

I'll prepare a short ops note to attach explaining the manifest generation and the HSM signing process.

— Rishi

From: Emma Li <emma.li@stratushealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Stratus Health Legal <legal@stratushealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Dec 2029 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mapping retention tiers to residency options — request

Ben/Laura/Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the appendix proposal. The matrix looks good overall and the suggested appendix language addresses most of our concerns. Two small follow-ups before we close: 1) Can you change the "2 year" audit log retention to "18 months" for high-fidelity logs? (we can negotiate archive terms separately), and 2) for the signed erasure confirmation, Stratus would like the HSM signature plus a machine-readable manifest (JSON) we can ingest into our records automation.

If those two items are acceptable we will sign the appendix and loop procurement for the order form. Appreciate the responsiveness — attaching the legal thumbs-up note from our counsel now.

Best,
Emma

--
Emma Li
Head of Vendor Risk, Stratus Health
